result.summary: GH-758 / ISS-0698 root cause: SUPERSEDED BY GH-752/ISS-0692 (commit 9d06bdf4 on main). The 'client hang after acquireIntegrationLock' symptom was caused by the pre-fix lock_timeout=90s + ambient statement_timeout=60s bracket around pg_advisory_lock, which 57014-cancelled the acquire under concurrent load (~50 binaries queueing). The error path was slow to propagate through build_runner IPC, presenting as a perceived hang. GH-752/ISS-0692 final fix zeroed both timeouts around the lock acquire. Branch base e9b1294d is post-9d06bdf4; symptom not reproducible (zig build test-integration-pin01 exits 0). All three plausible root causes listed in the prior OPEN analysis (panic / pg.Conn deadlock / memory error) are FALSE.

findings.description: Post-GH-752 code in tests/integration/helpers.zig wraps every pg_advisory_lock acquire with lock_timeout='0' AND statement_timeout='0'. Both timeouts are zeroed, so the acquire cannot be cancelled by 57014 nor 55P03. The 'client hang' symptom requires a 57014 statement_timeout cancellation during the lock wait -- which the current code cannot produce.

findings.description: All three plausible root causes in the prior OPEN analysis ((a) panic, (b) pg.Conn deadlock, (c) memory error) are FALSE. The actual cause was a 57014 statement_timeout cancellation during a contended pg_advisory_lock acquire, in code that has since been fixed. There is no panic, no deadlock, no memory error -- there was a pre-fix time-budget configuration that produced 57014 cancellation under contention.
